\section{Who Wrote and Who Checked the Proofs}\label{S-prov}
The proofs labelled \lab{S} in the main text were written by AI models and checked by AI models. No human referee has
read them yet. For each result, Tables~\ref{tab:provcore} and~\ref{tab:provring} say which model family wrote the text
that is printed here, which models checked it, whether a checker came from a different vendor than the writer, and
which programs recomputed facts. The vendors are Anthropic (Claude), OpenAI (Codex), and NVIDIA (Nemotron) and MiniMax, both run through
the Kilo tool; a few free models were run through the OpenCode tool under an alias, and for these the underlying model and
vendor are not recorded. The referee reports are not part of the anonymous code copy; we can supply them to the editor. Where a proof was corrected after a check, the
table says whether the corrected text was read again and by whom; ``final text read'' means the wording printed here.

\paragraph{What the checks found.}
The checks caught real errors in November 2026, all corrected. The main text said that the sum model re-splits a position and
then replaces components with a passed pawn; the engine and the theorem test the moved component first and split only if
no pawn is passed, and the two orders differ. The validity corollary was stated for both sides to move, but its
hypotheses can hold for one side only; it is now stated for the side to move. The certificate theorem said the punisher wins with one of its next moves, but the reply itself can
already be mate, so the clause now reads ``no later than''. The proof of Theorem~3.4 had one false sentence about which
moves win for Left. The printed proof of Theorem~1.11(c) had a gap in the move-count step. The proof of the wall rings (Section~\ref{S-wall}) named the wrong capture in one case of its Lemma~2 and had a gap in its Lemma~3; the lemmas themselves hold. The horizon-1 proposition was false on four ranks,
and promotion inside the pawn games had to be pinned down. An earlier proof, of the square-rule passer test, passed two AI
referees and was later refuted by a counterexample (Section~\ref{S-square}); we now state it as a computation.
These errors were found by AI checkers, and none of these checks replaces a human referee.

\emph{Limits.} All ring results rest on Lemmas~1--3 of Section~\ref{S-wall}, and the independent programs that support the
base cases were written by models from one description of the rules, so a shared misreading of the rules is not excluded.
